title: A free power can act or not act absolutely speaking, though not in the composite sense under God's efficacious will
source_text: XVI. Si quis autem urgeat esse de ratione potentiae liberae, ut positis omnibus requisitis ad operandum, possit operari & non operari: sed posito Decreto efficaci Dei praedeterminante nostrum liberum arbitrium ad operandum hoc in particulari, non posse voluntatem non operari illud, quia voluntati Dei nullus potest resistere: Respondet, de ratione potentiae liberae esse ut positis omnibus requisitis ad operandum, possit operari & non operari absolute & simpliciter loquendo: non tamen inconveniens esse, quod ex suppositione voluntatis Divinae efficacis, non possit in sensu composito non operari actum illum, ad quem praedeterminatur a Deo.
pass_a_gloss: XVI. But if anyone urges that it is of the nature of a free power that, all things requisite for working being posited, it can work and not work: but, an efficacious Decree of God being posited predetermining our free choice to work this in particular, the will cannot not work it, because no one can resist the will of God: He answers, that it is of the nature of a free power that, all things requisite for working being posited, it can work and not work absolutely and simply speaking: but yet it is not unfitting, that from the supposition of the efficacious Divine will, it cannot in the composite sense not work that act, to which it is predetermined by God.
pass_b_english: Someone may insist that a free power, by its nature, is able to act and not act once everything required for acting is in place. Yet once God's efficacious decree predetermines our free choice to do this particular thing, the will cannot fail to do it, for no one can resist God's will.

Alvarez answers that a free power, by its nature, is able to act and not act, with everything required for acting in place, speaking absolutely and without qualification. It is no absurdity, however, that granted God's efficacious will, it cannot in the composite sense fail to perform the act to which God predetermines it.

lemmas.gloss: all things requisite for working being posited
no one can resist the will of God

choices.why: The Schools' distinction between a proposition taken with its supposition (composite) and apart from it (divided); kept as technical terms.
